transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Ross (Redwood CSM), Aiden Zhou (Lyra Head of Procurement), Maya Singh (Lyra Security Lead), Carlos Vega (Dir Eng), Priya Nair (Lyra Legal), Eli Park (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen may be imperfect): discuss MSA/DPA redlines and onboarding steps; pricing for dedicated reserved capacity and SLAs; schedule benchmark.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Aiden: yep loud and clear, thanks Jordan. we have about 45 minutes, want to get through the legal ask and pricing and then next steps.
[00:12] Jordan: perfect. quick intros, i'm Jordan, i'll drive procurement questions and the MSA side; Sofia will cover technical and benchmarks.
[00:18] Sofia: hi all, thanks, i'll talk through the dedicated vs hosted perf and what we'll need for a cost/latency test.
[00:25] Maya: hi, I'm Maya, i focus on security, we have some questions on encryption and key mgmt.
[00:30] Carlos: Carlos here, will look after engineering acceptance and onprem options.
[00:33] Priya: Priya legal, i'll flag any DPA or contract concerns.
[00:36] Jordan: ok starting with the MSA/DPA — Priya, any immediate redlines on the DPA or special regs?
[00:42] Priya: we need explicit data residency language for eu data, plus KMS/HSM references; vendor indemnities are standard but want to see liability caps tied to fees. also we may request additional audit rights.
[00:52] Jordan: got it, our standard DPA includes regional residency and KMS options, but we can add explicit language. on liability caps we usually cap to 12 months of fees for hosted; for Dedicated enterprise contracts we can be flexible.
[01:05] Priya: ok flexibility appreciated, but procurement will push for higher cap if they store pii for customers.
[01:10] Aiden: timeline wise we need redlines back by end of week to hit procurement review next week, is that doable?
[01:15] Jordan: we'll aim to send a redline-friendly MSA+DPA by Tue/Thu — sorry, by 2027-09-28.
[01:20] Sofia: jumping into SLAs — for Dedicated we can commit to 99.95% uptime and per-call p99 latency targets; for Hosted API our published SLOs are a bit different.
[01:30] Eli: can you clarify p99 numbers? we need <150ms p99 for embeddings and <300ms p99 for 8k generation for our main customer flows.
[01:38] Sofia: so small correction, for embeddings the p99 can be around 120-180ms depending on batch sizing; gen depends on model and sequence length, but with Dedicated and optimized quantization we can get close to your targets. we'll validate in the benchmark.
[01:50] Carlos: is there a formal SLA penalty clause? procurement wants credit-based refunds for misses.
[01:55] Jordan: yes our enterprise SLA includes credits; standard formula is prorated credits up to X% of monthly fee subject to root cause analysis. can include in MSA.
[02:06] Priya: can you send sample SLA appendix?
[02:09] Jordan: yes will attach the SLA appendix and the formula; link to sample in our doc pack (shared after): [doc deck link]
[02:16] Maya: security: we need SOC2 type II report, ISO27001 cert, and architecture diagrams showing KMS integration and network separation for Dedicated. also we want to know where logs live and retention policies.
[02:27] Sofia: we will share SOC2 and ISO; for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering or private link; logs can be routed to your splunk or retained in Redwood logs with configurable retention.
[02:40] Maya: small note — transcription spelled red wood as two words earlier in our questionnaire, so i want that clarified.
[02:44] Jordan: haha noted, the product is Redwood, but fair call, transcripts sometimes break things.
[02:48] Aiden: about pricing — we're evaluating 1) Hosted pay-as-you-go 2) Dedicated reserved capacity monthly commit. what's typical break-even?
[02:57] Sofia: typically around sustained high throughput, Dedicated wins after you cross a threshold; we'll run numbers but example: for 100k reqs/day with medium prompt sizes, Dedicated reserved gives ~30-45% cost savings vs hosted list pricing.
[03:10] Carlos: do you support mixed routing? we might want cost-tier routing for non-prod traffic to hosted and prod to Dedicated.
[03:15] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports policies by route and model; can default to fallback if Dedicated capacity congested.
[03:21] Priya: any vendor onboarding docs or attestation we need to fill?
[03:25] Liam: yes we have a vendor questionnaire and an onboarding checklist; we'll send the questionnaire link and request responses from Maya, then we can move security review forward.
[03:33] Maya: expected timeline for security review? we have internal windows in early Oct.
[03:36] Jordan: we'll target to have docs in your hands by 2027-09-28, then aim to close reviews by 2027-10-05 if possible.
[03:44] Eli: technical note: for benchmarks we need to know hardware you're providing for Dedicated tests and whether we can provision a small cluster for the proof run.
[03:51] Sofia: we'll propose a test cluster spec (NVIDIA GH200 / H100 variants depending on region) and run both throughput and latency profiles. if you want onprem we can discuss packaging but that takes longer.
[04:04] Carlos: on-prem package, do you have air-gapped options?
[04:07] Sofia: yes, but that is a separate Private deployment track and usually involves professional services.
[04:12] Aiden: procurement will need cost scenarios including one-time onboarding fees, monthly reserved commit, and overage pricing.
[04:18] Jordan: i'll include onboarding fees in the spreadsheet; Sofia will map reserved tiers and projected savings.
[04:22] Priya: DPA question: do you support EU data only storage and processing?
[04:27] Jordan: yes we offer region pinning and can restrict processing to EU datacenters for Hosted; Dedicated we can colocate in region. we'll document residency language.
[04:36] Maya: also need to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys and ability to rotate keys without downtime. is that supported?
[04:42] Sofia: yes, customer-managed KMS supported; rotation procedure documented, for Dedicated we integrate with your KMS.
[04:48] Aiden: any other blockers from procurement? Priya?
[04:51] Priya: nothing major, just standard negotiating points re: liability cap and audit rights.
[04:55] Jordan: ok let's capture action items and owners — i'll send the MSA/DPA redline and SLA appendix, Sofia will prepare pricing and benchmark plan, Maya to send security questionnaire answers.
[05:03] Liam: i'll follow up with onboarding checklist and vendor questionnaire link.
[05:07] Aiden: we'll aim to review docs and get back within the week.
[05:10] Jordan: perfect. quick recap: send docs by 2027-09-28, benchmark week tentatively 2027-10-04, procurement decision expected early Oct.
[05:20] Carlos: thanks everyone.
[05:22] Priya: thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap and small transcription errors (product names, punctuation). References: shared deck and pricing spreadsheet will be provided post-call.
